terms: You build it, you run it
Dev team production ki ownership leti hai.
Dev aur Ops ke beech deewar.
def1.what:
Definition: DevOps ek culture + practices ka set hai jo development aur operations ko jodta hai taaki software tez, safe aur baar-baar deliver ho. CALMS framework adoption ko check karne ka tareeka hai.

Purane model mein dev code 'deewar ke upar se phenk' deta tha aur ops ko sambhalna padta tha.
def1.why: Chhote, frequent releases risk kam karte hain aur feedback jaldi milta hai.
def1.code:
# DevOps loop
plan -> code -> build -> test -> release -> deploy -> operate -> monitor -> (feedback) -> plan

# Example: har merge par
git push -> CI (build+test) -> CD (staging) -> canary -> prod -> alerts
gotchas: DevOps ek job title/tool nahi, culture hai
Automation bina measurement ke andhi hai
'DevOps team' banana naya silo ban sakta hai

terms: Ops ko software engineering se; SLOs, error budgets.
def2.what: Definition: DevOps 'kya aur kyun', SRE 'reliability ko measurable bana kar kaise' (SLI/SLO/error budget), Platform Engineering 'developers ke liye golden paths/portal' hai.
def2.why: Interview mein teeno ka fark aur overlap clear batana zaroori hai.
def2.code:
SLO: 99.9% requests < 300ms (30 days)
Error budget = 0.1% = ~43 min/month
Budget khatam -> feature releases roko, reliability work

Platform: `make service name=orders` -> repo + CI + k8s + dashboards ready
gotchas: SRE ≠ ops team ka naya naam
Error budget policy tabhi kaam karti jab management maane
Platform ko product ki tarah treat karo

def3.what: Definition: Plan → code → build → test → release → deploy → operate. Har stage automate; fast tests pehle, slow tests baad mein.
def3.why: Manual steps error aur delay laate hain.
def3.code:
stages: [lint, unit, build, integration, security, deploy-staging, e2e, deploy-prod]
# fast checks pehle: lint/unit < 5 min
gotchas: Flaky tests pipeline ka trust todte hain
Pipeline 10 min se upar ho to developers bypass karte hain

terms: Short-lived branches, main par frequent merge.
def4.what: Definition: Developers din mein kai baar main mein merge karte hain; incomplete features flags ke peeche. Release = flag on, deploy = code shipping — dono alag.
def4.why: Integration problems jaldi pakadte hain; CI/CD ke liye zaroori.

terms: Kitne deploys fail; recover kitne time mein.
def5.what: Definition: DORA ke 4 metrics: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore. Elite teams speed aur stability dono mein achhi hoti hain.
def5.why: Objectively dekhne ke liye ki delivery improve ho rahi hai ya nahi.
def5.code:
deploys/week = count(prod_deploys)
lead_time   = median(deploy_ts - first_commit_ts)
CFR         = failed_deploys / deploys
MTTR        = median(restore_ts - incident_ts)
cons: Individuals ko judge karne ke liye galat
gotchas: Goodhart's law: target banate hi gaming
Speed aur stability trade-off nahi, saath badhte hain

cic1.what: Definition: Build once, promote same artifact across environments (dev→staging→prod). Gates: tests, scans, approvals. Artifact immutable.
cic1.why: 'Staging mein chala, prod mein nahi' tab hota hai jab har env ke liye alag build ho.
cic1.code:
build -> image:sha-abc123 (ek baar)
deploy staging (image:sha-abc123 + staging config)
deploy prod    (image:sha-abc123 + prod config)

cic2.what: Definition: Events (push, PR) par jobs/steps chalte hain. Matrix builds, caching, secrets, reusable workflows, environments with approvals.
cic2.why: GitHub ke saath tight integration, setup kam.
cic2.code:
name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy: { matrix: { node: [18, 20] } }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci && npm test
gotchas: Secrets forks ko expose nahi hote

cic3.what: Definition: Blue/green instant rollback deta hai par double capacity. Canary real traffic par risk kam karta hai. Rolling default K8s strategy. A/B experiments ke liye.
cic3.why: Release risk aur downtime kam karne ke liye.
cic3.code:
# Argo Rollouts canary
steps:
  - setWeight: 5
  - pause: { duration: 10m }
  - setWeight: 25
  - analysis: success-rate > 99%
  - setWeight: 100

cic4.what: Definition: Har build ek versioned artifact (image digest/SHA). Immutable tags, signed, retention policy, vulnerability scan registry mein.
cic4.why: Jo test hua wahi prod mein jaye — traceability.
cic4.code:
docker build -t registry/app:1.4.2-abc123 .
docker push registry/app:1.4.2-abc123
cosign sign registry/app@sha256:...
# k8s: image digest se pin
gotchas: Retention policy nahi to storage cost

cic5.what: Definition: Pipeline mein secrets scan, SAST, SCA, container scan, DAST, signing aur provenance (SLSA). Pipeline khud bhi attack target hai — least privilege tokens.
cic5.why: Supply chain attacks build system se aate hain.
cic5.code:
- gitleaks
- semgrep
- trivy image app:sha
- syft -> sbom
- cosign sign
# OIDC se short-lived cloud creds (long-lived keys nahi)
gotchas: Gate failure ko ignore karne ka tareeka na ho
PR from forks ko secrets nahi

terms: Union filesystem — layers stack + writable top layer.
doc1.what: Definition: Image layers ka stack hai, container = image + writable layer. Layers cache aur share hote hain. Containers namespaces (isolation) aur cgroups (resource limits) use karte hain.
doc1.why: Layer samajhna build speed aur image size optimize karne ki jad hai.
doc1.code:
$ docker history app:1.0          # layers dekho
$ docker run -m 256m --cpus=0.5 app   # cgroup limits
$ docker inspect app | jq '.[0].GraphDriver'
cons: Shared kernel — VM jitna isolated nahi
gotchas: Delete karne se bhi pichli layer ka data image mein rehta hai
Writable layer ephemeral — volumes use karo

terms: Build stage alag, runtime stage chhota.
doc2.what: Definition: Dependencies pehle copy+install, phir source — cache hit zyada. Multi-stage se compilers final image mein nahi. .dockerignore, non-root user, pinned versions.
doc2.why: Chhoti image = fast pull, kam attack surface.
doc2.code:
FROM node:20 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
USER node
CMD ["node","dist/main.js"]
gotchas: COPY . . pehle likhne se cache toot-ta hai
Secrets build args mein mat daalo

terms: Container host network share karta hai.
doc3.what: Definition: Bridge network par containers apas mein naam se baat karte hain (user-defined bridge). Ports publish karke bahar. K8s mein CNI plugins pod networking dete hain.
doc3.why: Connectivity issues debug karna aur isolation design.
doc3.code:
$ docker network create appnet
$ docker run -d --network appnet --name db postgres
$ docker run -d --network appnet -p 8080:8080 api   # api -> db:5432
$ docker run --network host nginx   # port mapping nahi
gotchas: localhost container ke andar apna hi hota hai
Default bridge par DNS naam nahi
-p publish ke bina bahar se access nahi

doc4.what: Definition: Root user, privileged mode, docker.sock mount avoid. Read-only rootfs, capabilities drop, seccomp default profile, resource limits.
doc4.why: Container escape se host compromise ho sakta hai.

doc5.what: Definition: docker-compose.yml mein app + DB + cache ek command se. Local dev aur integration tests ke liye perfect; production orchestration nahi.
doc5.why: 'Mere machine par chalta hai' hatane ka sabse aasaan tareeka.
gotchas: depends_on ready hone ka wait nahi karta — healthcheck
Volume delete karoge to data jaayega

k8s1.what: Definition: Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager. Nodes: kubelet, container runtime, kube-proxy. Declarative model: desired state likho, controllers actual ko match karte hain.
k8s1.why: Failures (pod pending, node not ready) debug karne ke liye architecture samajhna zaroori.
k8s1.code:
$ kubectl get nodes
$ kubectl describe pod web-1      # events: scheduling, pull, probe
$ kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

k8s2.what: Definition: Deployment ReplicaSet ke through pods manage karta hai. Service label selector se pods ko load-balance karta hai. ConfigMap config, Secret sensitive (base64, encrypted nahi by default).

k8s3.what: Definition: Service types: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer. Ingress controller (nginx) HTTP routing deta hai. Har pod ka apna IP; CNI pod-to-pod connectivity deta hai.
k8s3.why: Traffic flow aur outside exposure samajhne ke liye.
k8s3.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
spec:
  rules:
  - host: api.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: web, port: { number: 80 } } }
gotchas: Ingress resource ke liye controller install hona chahiye
Pod IP ephemeral — Service use karo

k8s4.what: Definition: Helm templating se same manifests alag environments mein; Operators (jaise Postgres operator) domain knowledge (backup, failover) automate karte hain.
k8s4.why: Bade manifests ko manage aur stateful apps ko run karna.
k8s4.code:
$ helm install web ./chart -f values-prod.yaml
$ helm upgrade --install web ./chart --set image.tag=1.2.1
$ helm rollback web 1
$ helm template ./chart | kubectl diff -f -

k8s5.what: Definition: Least-privilege RBAC, default-deny NetworkPolicy, Pod Security Admission, secrets encryption/external secrets, image policies, audit logs.
k8s5.why: Default K8s mein sab pods sab se baat kar sakte hain.
k8s5.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: { name: default-deny }
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
# phir specific allow rules
gotchas: NetworkPolicy ke liye CNI support chahiye
ServiceAccount token auto-mount band karo jahan zaroorat nahi

terms: Config aur real resources ka mapping.
iac1.what: Definition: Terraform HCL mein desired infra declare karta hai. plan diff dikhata hai, apply change karta hai, state file track karti hai.
iac1.why: Infra versioned, reviewable aur reproducible ban jaata hai.
gotchas: State file mein secrets ho sakte hain
plan review ke bina apply mat karo

iac2.what: Definition: Team ke liye state remote + locked + encrypted. Drift detection scheduled terraform plan se. State split per environment/component.
iac2.why: Local state par teams ek-dusre ka kaam overwrite kar deti hain.
gotchas: Bahut bada state slow — split karo

iac3.what: Definition: Config management servers ke andar software/config manage karta hai. Ansible SSH se; Terraform provisioning ke liye, Ansible configuration ke liye.
iac3.why: Servers ko manually configure karna error-prone hai.
iac3.code:
- hosts: web
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: nginx install
      apt: { name: nginx, state: present }
    - name: service on
      service: { name: nginx, state: started, enabled: true }
gotchas: Idempotency ke liye modules use karo, shell kam

iac4.what: Definition: Change = naya image build → naye instances launch → purane terminate. Snowflake servers aur drift khatam.
gotchas: Image mein secrets bake mat karo

terms: Cluster khud Git se kheenchta hai.
iac5.what: Definition: Deploy = Git commit/PR. Controller continuously desired state vs live compare karke sync karta hai. Audit trail, rollback = git revert.
iac5.why: CI ko cluster credentials nahi dene padte; drift auto-correct.
gotchas: App repo aur config repo alag rakho
manual kubectl edit revert ho jaayega

pro1.what: Definition: HPA CPU/custom metrics (RPS, queue depth) par pods scale karta hai. Nodes ke liye Cluster Autoscaler/Karpenter. Load test se baseline set karo.
pro1.why: Traffic spikes mein availability aur off-peak cost saving.
pro1.code:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { kind: Deployment, name: web }
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 30
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: { name: cpu, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 65 } }
gotchas: Requests set na ho to HPA kaam nahi karta
HPA + VPA same metric par conflict
Scale-up delay ke liye min replicas buffer

terms: Backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active.
pro2.what: Definition: RPO/RTO business tay karta hai; strategy uske hisaab se (cost badhta jaata hai). Backups ka restore test karna zaroori.
pro2.code:
RPO 24h/RTO 24h -> backup & restore
RPO 1h/RTO 1h   -> pilot light
RPO ~0/RTO min  -> multi-region active-active
aws rds restore-db-instance-to-point-in-time ...   # drill karo
gotchas: Backups same region/account mein na ho

pro3.what: Definition: Production-jaisi conditions mein controlled failures (pod kill, latency inject, AZ outage) se weaknesses dhundna. Hypothesis → experiment → learn → fix.
pro3.why: Failure real hone se pehle resilience prove karna.
pro3.code:
# Chaos Mesh / Litmus / Gremlin / AWS FIS
kind: PodChaos
spec: { action: pod-kill, mode: one, selector: { labelSelectors: { app: web } } }
# abort conditions + monitoring ready

terms: Cluster mein enter hone se pehle check.
pro4.what: Definition: Policies code mein: 'koi privileged pod nahi', 'images sirf trusted registry se', 'S3 public nahi'. CI aur admission controller dono par enforce; audit evidence auto.
pro4.code:
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: no-latest
    match: { any: [{ resources: { kinds: [Pod] } }] }
    validate:
      message: latest tag not allowed
      pattern: { spec: { containers: [{ image: "!*:latest" }] } }
gotchas: Audit mode se shuru, phir enforce

aws1.what: Definition: EC2 virtual servers. Purchasing: On-Demand, Reserved/Savings Plans, Spot. Key pair SSH ke liye (ya SSM Session Manager better). ASG scaling.
aws1.why: AWS compute ka base; interview mein basic.
aws1.code:
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-xxx --instance-type t3.micro \
  --security-group-ids sg-123 --iam-instance-profile Name=app-role
# SSH ke bajaye: aws ssm start-session --target i-abc

aws2.what: Definition: S3 11 9s durability. Versioning, lifecycle (IA/Glacier), SSE-KMS, Block Public Access, presigned URLs direct upload/download ke liye.
aws2.why: Misconfigured S3 buckets ke breaches famous hain.
cons: Eventual list semantics (ab strong), request costs

aws3.what: Definition: RDS managed backups, patching, failover. Multi-AZ availability ke liye, read replicas performance ke liye — dono alag cheezein.
aws3.why: Database ops offload, par design decisions phir bhi aapke.
aws3.code:
aws rds create-db-instance --engine postgres --multi-az --storage-encrypted \
  --backup-retention-period 7 --db-instance-class db.t3.medium ...
# app connection pooling (RDS Proxy) lambda ke liye

terms: Naye execution environment ka startup delay.
aws4.what: Definition: Lambda event aane par code chalata hai, per-invocation billing. Limits: 15 min, memory 10GB. Provisioned concurrency cold start kam karta hai.
aws4.why: Spiky/event-driven workloads mein ops aur cost bachta hai.
gotchas: SQS retries se duplicate — idempotent banao

aws5.what: Definition: VPC mein CIDR, subnets (multi-AZ), route tables, IGW (internet), NAT GW (private se bahar), VPC endpoints (AWS services bina internet).
gotchas: CIDR overlap peering block karta hai

aws6.what: Definition: Users ke liye SSO/MFA, workloads ke liye roles (instance profile, IRSA), long-lived access keys avoid. Explicit Deny > Allow. Access Analyzer unused permissions batata hai.
gotchas: Root user MFA aur use nahi

aws7.what: Definition: CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards. Custom metrics, composite alarms. Memory/disk ke liye agent chahiye.
aws7.why: Observability ke bina incident detect nahi hota.
aws7.code:
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name 5xx-high --metric-name HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count \
  --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --statistic Sum --period 60 --evaluation-periods 5 \
  --threshold 50 --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold --alarm-actions $SNS_ARN
# Logs Insights: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /ERROR/ | limit 20

aws8.what: Definition: ALB path/host routing, WebSocket, WAF integration. Health checks unhealthy targets nikalte hain. Connection draining deployments mein.
aws8.code:
TargetGroup: health check GET /health -> 200, interval 10s, healthy 2, unhealthy 3
Listener 443: /api/* -> tg-api ; default -> tg-web
deregistration_delay = 30s
gotchas: Health check endpoint DB-heavy na ho
Sticky sessions scaling hurt karti hain

serverless.what: Definition: Serverless mein infra management provider ka; auto-scale, per-ms billing. Patterns: API GW+Lambda, S3→Lambda, queue workers, step functions.
serverless.code:
API Gateway -> Lambda -> DynamoDB
S3 upload -> Lambda -> thumbnail
SQS -> Lambda (batch, DLQ)
Step Functions: orchestration
gotchas: Steady high traffic par containers sasti ho sakti hain

cloud-networking.what: Definition: Public/private subnets, SG vs NACL, LB layers (L4/L7), DNS (Route53), CDN, VPN/peering/Transit Gateway.
cloud-networking.code:
Internet -> CloudFront -> ALB (public) -> ECS (private) -> RDS (private)
SG chain: alb-sg -> app-sg -> db-sg
gotchas: SG referencing SG use karo, IP nahi
DNS TTL failover ko slow karta hai

terms: Instance size usage ke hisaab se.
cost-optimization.what: Definition: Pehle visibility (tags, Cost Explorer), phir right-size, idle resources delete, commitment discounts steady load par, spot fault-tolerant workloads par, storage tiering, data transfer kam.
cost-optimization.code:
Tag: team, env, service  -> cost allocation
Compute Optimizer / Trust Advisor se rightsizing
Spot for batch/CI; On-demand + savings plan for baseline
S3 lifecycle -> IA/Glacier; delete unattached EBS/IPs
gotchas: NAT aur data transfer hidden costs

feature-flags.what: Definition: Flags runtime par behaviour badalte hain bina deploy. Use: gradual rollout, A/B, kill switch, ops toggles. Flag ka lifecycle: create → rollout → cleanup.
gotchas: Flag service down hone par fallback
